classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the explicitly taught initial-volume constant-rate model to an emptying tank, tabulate, graph and state the finite-domain formula; stages supplied.

content.prompt: A tank can hold up to $50$ litres of water. It is full to start with. Water is flowing slowly out at a rate of $5$ litres per minute.

inlines.text: Prepare a table of values showing how much water is in the tank at 1-minute intervals.

answer.worked: At time 0 the tank contains 50 L, and every minute 5 L leaves. Thus the values for t=0 through 10 are 50,45,40,35,30,25,20,15,10,5,0 L.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Plot the graph of the volume $V$ (in litres) of water in the tank against time $t$ (in minutes) since the start.

answer.worked: Every minute the volume decreases by 5 L. The graph is the straight line segment from $(0,50)$ to $(10,0)$.

spec.description: Complete labelled constant-rate coordinate graph. Solid/dashed styles distinguish source travellers; all source-defined finite domains preserved.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Give the formula for $V$ in terms of $t$.

answer.worked: Start with 50 L and subtract 5 L for each minute: $V=50-5t$. The tank is empty at t=10, so $0\le t\le10$.
